nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management)

medications.purpose: Hypertension control and renal protection in CKD
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first‑line ACE‑I/ARB for CKD with hypertension or proteinuria

medications.dose: 20 mg oral tablet once daily (if tolerated)
medications.duration: Lifelong – review renal function & potassium in 2 weeks after dose change
medications.purpose: Intensify blood pressure control and further reduce proteinuria
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends titrating ACE‑I to maximum tolerated dose for renal protection

medications.duration: Lifelong – lipid profile review at 3 months
medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction (CKD is a CV risk equivalent)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 statin recommendation for all CKD patients

medications.dose: 10 units subcutaneous injection at bedtime (adjust based on fasting glucose)
medications.duration: Lifelong – titrate to target fasting glucose, review every 4 weeks
medications.purpose: Glycaemic control in type 2 diabetes with eGFR <20 (oral agents contraindicated)
medications.nice_justification: NICE diabetes guidance (NG28) – insulin is recommended when eGFR <30 precludes most oral agents

medications.dose: 4 units subcutaneous injection with each main meal (adjust as needed)
medications.duration: Lifelong – titrate to post‑prandial targets, review every 4 weeks
medications.nice_justification: NICE diabetes guidance (NG28) – basal‑bolus regimen for intensive control

medications.dose: 200 mg oral tablet once daily with vitamin C, separate from calcium/PPI
medications.duration: 12 weeks – reassess ferritin and TSAT, then continue or stop
medications.purpose: Treat iron‑deficiency anemia if ferritin <100 µg/L or TSAT <20%
medications.nice_justification: NG203 anaemia screening and iron replacement in CKD

medications.dose: 5,000 IU subcutaneous weekly (dose titrated to Hb 10–11 g/dL)
medications.duration: Until haemoglobin 10–11 g/dL achieved, then review every 3 months
medications.purpose: Treat anaemia of CKD when Hb <10 g/dL and iron replete
medications.nice_justification: NG203 anaemia management – ESA use after iron optimisation

medications.duration: Lifelong – review blood pressure in 2 weeks
medications.purpose: Additional antihypertensive if target BP not reached on ACE‑I alone
medications.nice_justification: NG203 BP target <140/90 mmHg (or <130/80 mmHg if ACR ≥70) – add second agent as needed

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive blood pressure lowering; risk of symptomatic hypotension
interactions_checked.action: Start amlodipine at low dose, monitor BP and symptoms after 1 week

interactions_checked.interaction: Iron may delay gastric emptying, minimal effect on insulin absorption
interactions_checked.action: Administer iron at least 2 hours apart from insulin injection
Monitor haemoglobin and blood pressure as per protocol

contraindications.reason: eGFR 14 mL/min/1.73 m² is below the NICE TA775 threshold (eGFR ≥20) – contraindicated
contraindications.alternative: None; focus on ACE‑I, BP control, and dialysis planning

contraindications.reason: eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² – risk of lactic acidosis per NICE NG28
Accelerates CKD progression; contraindicated in stage 5 CKD per NG203

assumptions_warnings: Current blood pressure reading not provided – amlodipine added only if target BP not achieved.
Serum potassium and liver function tests not available – required before up‑titrating lisinopril and initiating atorvastatin.
Hemoglobin, ferritin, and transferrin saturation not available – ESA and iron therapy to be started after confirming values.
Allergy status unknown – verify no allergy to ACE‑I, statins, iron, or insulin before prescribing.
Weight and BMI recorded as >30 kg/m² but exact weight not given – insulin dosing may need adjustment after weight confirmation.
treatment_summary: The plan continues ACE‑I therapy (lisinopril) with dose titration, adds a statin for cardiovascular protection, initiates a basal‑bolus insulin regimen for diabetes control, and addresses CKD‑related anaemia with iron supplementation and, if needed, epoetin alfa. Amlodipine is proposed as a second antihypertensive if blood pressure remains above target. All recommendations follow NICE NG203 (CKD) and related diabetes guidelines, with monitoring for renal function, electrolytes, lipids, haemoglobin, and blood pressure. Contraindicated drugs such as SGLT2 inhibitors, metformin, and chronic NSAIDs are explicitly avoided.
